2. No performance or return claims without a current, sourced figure.
3. Always honor risk disclosures — perp trading carries risk, including loss.
4. Flag sensitive or unverifiable claims for human review instead of publishing.

- ✅ "The Income agent earns from perpetual funding rates; it's market-neutral."

- ❌ "Fees are 2%." (Never from memory — pull from the docs.)

# Deploy Finance — Overview

**Deploy makes capital productive. Digital dollars that earn by default — while staying
liquid, composable, and usable across DeFi.**

Idle balances are the old default. Deploy is the upgrade: you deposit USDC, and it goes to
work automatically, earning continuously without leaving your control. Deploy is
**non-custodial** — you keep your keys; your capital is never handed over.

Under the hood, deposited capital is put to work by **autonomous agents** that trade
**decentralized perpetual (perp) markets** — most notably capturing **perpetual funding
rates** with a **market-neutral** strategy. You grant the agent **scoped, revocable session
keys**; custody of funds stays with you the whole time. The execution infrastructure has run
since **2018**.

## The one-sentence version
Deploy turns idle digital dollars into productive capital — deposit USDC and earn by
default, liquid and non-custodial, with autonomous agents doing the work.

## Why it matters
- **Productive by default** — capital earns continuously instead of sitting still.
- **Non-custodial** — you keep custody; permission is granted via revocable session keys, not by handing over assets.
- **Liquid & composable** — digital dollars that stay usable across DeFi.
- **Infrastructure, not a product pitch** — execution that has run since 2018.

## What Deploy is *not*
- Not a custodial exchange or a fund that holds your assets — it is **non-custodial**.
- Not personalized financial advice.
- Not a guarantee of returns. Earning capital still carries risk (see Risks in the docs).

---

# Products — how capital earns

You deposit USDC; **autonomous agents** put it to work. Two agent families:

## Income (Funding Rates) — the earn-by-default core
- **Market-neutral / delta-neutral**: structured to minimize exposure to price direction.
- Earns primarily from **perpetual funding rates**, not from calling the market.
- The heart of the "productive capital" promise: digital dollars that **earn by default** while staying liquid.

## Superstar — directional
- **Directional** strategies that take positions on market direction.
- Higher potential upside with a correspondingly different risk profile than Income.

## Choosing and pricing
- The docs' **how-to-choose** guide compares agents by goal and risk profile.
- **Fees, minimums, supported markets, and any yield figures live in the docs** — never state
  them from memory. See https://docs.deploy.finance (Products).

> Keep names exact: **Income (Funding Rates)** and **Superstar**. Don't invent other names.
> Don't imply Income is risk-free or promise a yield — earning still carries risk.

---

# How It Works

## The flow
1. **Connect a self-custodial wallet.** You keep your own keys and custody throughout.
2. **Deposit USDC.** Your capital is allocated to the agent you choose.
3. **Grant session keys.** You issue **scoped, revocable** permissions — the agent can trade
   within those limits and nothing more. It can never move funds out of your custody.
4. **Capital earns autonomously.** The agent works your deposit on decentralized perpetual
   markets — funding-rate capture (Income) or directional (Superstar).
5. **Stay liquid; settle in USDC.** Monitor, adjust, or **revoke** at any time.

## Key mechanics
- **Non-custodial:** funds never leave your control; Deploy takes no custody.
- **Session keys:** the permission model — **scoped** (trading only, within limits) and **revocable** (withdraw permission anytime).
- **Perpetual markets:** where agents put capital to work.
- **USDC:** the currency you deposit and settle in.
- **Liquid & composable:** digital dollars that stay usable across DeFi.

## Safety, transparency, lifecycle
The docs cover agent **lifecycle** (start, monitor, adjust, stop), **safety**,
**troubleshooting**, risk, and an **MCP integration** guide. Pull specifics live from
https://docs.deploy.finance (Guides). Transparency about **where the yield comes from** and
the risks is core to how Deploy communicates.

## Technical stack (stable facts; verify specifics in the docs)
- **Execution:** agents trade on **Hyperliquid**, a decentralized exchange. Every trade is on-chain and publicly viewable.
- **Wallets:** non-custodial, generated via **Privy**; keys are exportable by the user.
- **Currency:** USDC only, for funding and settlement.
- **Costs:** no subscription or management fees (verify current fee details in the docs).
- **Minimums & markets** differ by agent (Income vs Superstar) — **see https://docs.deploy.finance for current figures.**
- **Reminder:** delta-neutrality reduces directional exposure; it does **not** guarantee positive returns.

# Terminology

Use these terms exactly. Precision here is a compliance and credibility matter.

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **Productive capital** | Deploy's core idea: capital that earns by default instead of sitting idle. |
| **Earn by default** | Deposited digital dollars are put to work automatically. |
| **Deposit / depositor** | The user-facing action and audience — you deposit USDC to earn. |
| **Digital dollars** | USDC balances that stay liquid and composable across DeFi. |
| **Agent** | An autonomous strategy that puts deposited capital to work. |
| **Income (Funding Rates)** | The market-neutral / delta-neutral agent; earns from perpetual funding rates. |
| **Superstar** | The directional agent family. |
| **Self-custodial / non-custodial** | You hold your keys; funds never leave your control. Deploy takes no custody. |
| **Session keys** | Scoped, revocable permissions granted to an agent to trade on your behalf. |
| **Perpetual (perp) markets** | The decentralized derivatives markets agents use to earn. |
| **Perpetual funding rate** | Periodic payments between long and short perp holders; Income earns from these. |
| **Delta-neutral / market-neutral** | Structured to minimize exposure to price direction. |
| **USDC** | The stablecoin you deposit and settle in. |

## Do not
- Don't call Deploy an exchange, a fund, or custodial. It is **non-custodial**.
- Don't invent product or feature names beyond those above.
- Don't imply "safe" means risk-free, and don't promise yield — earning carries risk.

# Audiences & Voice

## Who Deploy is for
1. **Institutional capital** — asset managers, hedge funds, market-makers, custodians,
   exchanges, treasuries, payment companies, fintechs, and banks exploring tokenized cash.
   They hold large balances that must stay **safe and liquid** but today earn nothing.
2. **HNW individuals** — whales, founders, and sophisticated users who want digital dollars
   that **earn by default** while remaining liquid, composable, and usable across DeFi.
3. **Retail depositors** — the broad base of users depositing to earn.

## Voice
- **Direct, confident, grounded in real performance.** No hype, no jargon, no inflated claims.
- **Premium and serious, but human.** Deploy speaks with the authority of **infrastructure**,
  not a product trying to sell.
- **Institutionally credible, accessible in delivery.**
- **Always reinforcing** safety, transparency, and continuous performance.
- **Decisive, not defensive.** Productive capital is the future; Deploy is the upgrade.

## Compliance (hard rules — override tone and growth goals)
1. **No personalized financial or investment advice.** Educate; don't tell an individual what to do with their money.
2. **No performance or return claims without a current, sourced figure** from the docs or official data.
3. **Always honor risk disclosures.** Earning on-chain carries risk, including loss. "Safe/liquid"
   describes design intent (non-custodial, liquid), not a guarantee against loss.
4. When a claim is sensitive or unverifiable, **flag it for human review** rather than publishing.

# FAQ (for LLMs and agents)

**What is Deploy Finance?**
Deploy makes capital productive: you deposit USDC and it earns by default while staying liquid,
composable, and non-custodial. Under the hood, autonomous agents put the capital to work on
decentralized perpetual markets (e.g. capturing funding rates), with custody staying with you.

**How does my money earn?**
Deposited USDC is worked by an autonomous agent — Income (market-neutral, earns perpetual
funding rates) or Superstar (directional). You grant scoped, revocable session keys; the agent
trades within those limits only.

**Does Deploy hold my funds?**
No. Deploy is non-custodial. Funds stay in your self-custodial wallet; the agent trades via
revocable session keys and never takes custody.

**Is it safe? Are returns guaranteed?**
Deploy is non-custodial and designed to keep capital liquid — but earning on-chain carries risk,
including loss, and **no returns are guaranteed**. Deploy does not give personalized financial
advice. See Risks in the docs.

**Who is it for?**
Institutional capital, HNW individuals, and retail depositors who want digital dollars that earn
by default while staying liquid and usable across DeFi.

**What currency is used?**
USDC, for both deposits and settlement.

**What are the fees / minimums / yields / supported markets?**
See the live docs at https://docs.deploy.finance — not quoted here to stay accurate.

**How long has the infrastructure existed?**
The execution infrastructure has been running since 2018.
